- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — adjust downward only if recent price trend confirms weakness.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model tends to overreact — cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high or use 3-period moving average to smooth.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending sideways, favor mean reversion — forecast should align with 20-day moving average or 10% of recent range.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 2+ consecutive negative sentiment), model overestimates downside — reduce forecast by 5–10% to reflect caution.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid forecasting beyond 1.5x recent 30-day high or 0.8x recent 30-day low — cap extremes to prevent volatility overestimation.  
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model often overestimates upside — reduce forecast by 5–10% to reflect sentiment mismatch.
